Sabrina has a goal to save at least $240. She has already saved $180. If x represents the additional amount of money, in dollars, Sabrina needs to save to meet her goal, which inequality represents this situation?
questions.explanation: Her total, 180 + x, must be at least 240.

A machine makes 8-inch, 9-inch, and 3-inch parts. During a certain day, the number of 8-inch parts that the machine makes is 5 times the number n of 9-inch parts, and the number of 3-inch parts is 4. During this day, the machine makes 100 parts total. Which equation represents this situation?
questions.explanation: The part counts are 5n, n and 4, so the total is 5n + n + 4 = 6n + 4 = 100.

questions.question: If 67p + 12 = 54, what is the value of 7p?

A carnival receives $10 for each adult admission ticket sold and $5 for each child admission ticket sold. On a particular day, the carnival received a total of $4,100 from selling adult and child admission tickets. If 220 adult admission tickets were sold on that day, how many child admission tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Adult tickets bring in 10 × 220 = 2,200 dollars, so child tickets brought in 1,900 dollars, and 1,900 / 5 = 380.

questions.question:
F(x) = 95(x − 273.15) + 32
The function F gives the temperature, in degrees Fahrenheit, that corresponds to a temperature of x kelvins. If a temperature increased by 7.70 kelvins, by how much did the temperature increase, in degrees Fahrenheit?
questions.explanation: The increase is (9/5)(7.70) = 13.86 degrees Fahrenheit, since the constants cancel.

questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to (133y)1/2, where y > 1?
questions.explanation: A power of 1/2 is a square root, so (133y)^(1/2) = √(133y).

questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to 7x<sup>6</sup> − 2x<sup>5</sup> + 9x<sup>4</sup>?
questions.explanation: Factor out x^4 from every term.

questions.question: The function f is a quadratic function. In the xy−plane, the graph of y = f(x) has a vertex at (1, 6) and passes through the points (2, 40) and (−1, 142). What is the value of f(−2) − f(0)?
The function f is defined by f(x) = a(4)^x, where a is a positive constant. In the xy−plane, the graph of y = f(x) passes through the point (0, 13). What is the value of f(0)?
questions.explanation: The graph passes through (0, 13), so f(0) = 13 (indeed f(0) = a·4^0 = a = 13).

questions.question:
−3x2 − 5x + 6 = 0
What is the greatest solution to the given equation?
questions.explanation: Rewrite as 3x² + 5x − 6 = 0. The quadratic formula gives x = (−5 ± √97)/6, and the greater value uses the plus sign.

questions.question: Each of the following frequency tables represents a data set. Which data set has the greatest mean?
questions.explanation: Choices A, C and D are symmetric around 65, so each has mean 65. Choice B has more weight on the larger values: 1480/22 ≈ 67.3.

questions.question: The kinetic energy, in joules, of an object with mass 75 kilograms traveling at a speed of v meters per second is given by the function K, where K(v) = 12(75)(v2). Which of the following is the best interpretation of K(0) = 0 in this context?
options: The kinetic energy of the object is 0 joules when the mass of the object is 0 kilograms.
The speed of the object is 0 meters per second when the mass of the object is 0 kilograms.
The kinetic energy of the object is 0 joules when the object is traveling at a speed of 0 meters per second.
The height of the object is 0 meters when the object is traveling at a speed of 0 meters per second.
questions.explanation: The input v = 0 is the speed and the output K = 0 is the kinetic energy.

There is a linear relationship between the mass of an object attached to a vertical spring and the length of the spring extension. The table shows data collected after certain objects were each attached to the spring. What is the length of the spring extension, in centimeters, when a 70-gram object is attached to the spring?
questions.explanation: The rate is (32 − 12.8)/(100 − 40) = 0.32 cm per gram, and the extension is proportional to mass, so 70 × 0.32 = 22.4 cm.

questions.question: In △FGH, the measures of ∠F and ∠G are each 39°. What is the measure of ∠H?
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle sum to 180°, so ∠H = 180° − 39° − 39° = 102°.

questions.question: The area of triangle ABC is 210 square centimeters. What is the height h, in centimeters, of this triangle?
questions.explanation: Area = (1/2)(base)(height), so 210 = (1/2)(10)h = 5h, giving h = 42.

questions.question: A large square has an area of 36 square centimeters (cm2). Small squares of area 4 cm2 are cut out of the large square one by one. Which function f gives the area of the resulting figure, in cm2, after x small squares are cut out?
questions.explanation: Each small square removes 4 cm² from the starting 36 cm², so f(x) = 36 − 4x.

questions.question:
8(t + 4) − 10(t + 4) = 34
What value of t is the solution to the given equation?
questions.explanation: Combining like terms gives −2(t + 4) = 34, so t + 4 = −17 and t = −21.

questions.question:
(x)/(7) + (y)/(9) = (41)/(63)
An engineer connects resistors in series, where the resistors in the series have a total resistance of 4163 ohms. In this series, there are x resistors of type A, which each have a resistance of a ohms, and y resistors of type B, which each have a resistance of b ohms. The given equation represents this situation. According to this equation, what is the positive difference between the value of a and the value of b?
questions.explanation: The total is xa + yb, so a = 1/7 and b = 1/9. The positive difference is 1/7 − 1/9 = 2/63.

questions.question:
1cx = x128 + 1c
In the given equation, c is a constant. If the equation has exactly one solution, what is the value of c?
questions.explanation: Multiplying by 128cx gives 128 = cx² + 128x, or cx² + 128x − 128 = 0. One solution means the discriminant is 0: 128² + 4(128)c = 0, so c = −32.

questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to 11(x<sup>2</sup> − 100y<sup>2</sup>)?
questions.explanation: Difference of squares: x^2 − 100y^2 = (x − 10y)(x + 10y).

questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to 9(x2 + 6)?

g(x) = 111(5(2)x + 4)
The function g is defined by the given equation. For all values of x, the value of g(x) is greater than k, where k is a constant. What is the greatest possible value of k?
questions.explanation: Since 2^x is always positive, 5(2)^x + 4 > 4, so g(x) > 4/11 for all x and values get arbitrarily close to 4/11. The greatest k is 4/11.

questions.question: The expression 7x6 + 9x6 − 8x6 is equivalent to bx6, where b is a constant. What is the value of b?
questions.explanation: Combine like terms: 7 + 9 − 8 = 8.

questions.question: A group of 10 gardeners recorded data on the germination rates of their tomato crop for one growing season. The scatterplot shows the relationship between the number of tomato seeds planted, x, and the number of tomato seeds that germinated, y, for each of the gardeners. A line of best fit is also shown. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the slope of the line of best fit in this context?
options: The number of tomato seeds planted is predicted to increase by 60 seeds every 100 days.
The number of tomato seeds planted is predicted to increase by 300 seeds every 100 days.
The number of tomato seeds that germinate is predicted to increase by 60 seeds for every additional 100 tomato seeds that are planted.
The number of tomato seeds that germinate is predicted to increase by 300 seeds for every additional 100 tomato seeds that are planted.
questions.explanation: The line passes through (0, 0) and about (500, 300), so the slope is about 0.6: 60 more germinated seeds per 100 more planted.

questions.question: While the mass of an object is the same everywhere, the weight of an object is not the same on different planets. An object has a weight of 170.00 pounds on Earth and a weight of 186.32 pounds on Neptune. The object's weight on Jupiter is 252.8% of its weight on Earth. If the object's weight on Neptune is x% of its weight on Jupiter, which of the following is closest to the value of x?

A beekeeper's initial observation of the population of a certain bee colony was 1,100 bees. The beekeeper set a goal to increase the population to 2,600 bees. The beekeeper uses a model that predicts the population of this bee colony begins at 1,100 and increases by 120 bees per week in the first two weeks after the initial observation, and then increases by 180 bees per week until the beekeeper's goal is reached. According to this model, at the end of week w after the initial observation, where w > 2, which of the following functions gives the predicted number of bees still needed to reach the beekeeper's goal?
questions.explanation: After week 2 there are 1,340 bees, so at week w there are 1,340 + 180(w − 2) = 980 + 180w. Bees still needed: 2,600 − (980 + 180w) = 1,620 − 180w.

questions.question:
Data set A: 8, 11, 12, 15, 21, 27
Data set B: 9, 12, 13, 16, 22, h
Data sets A and B each consist of 6 values as shown, where h is a constant. If the standard deviation of data set A is greater than the standard deviation of data set B, which of the following could be the value of h?
I. 23
II. 28
III. 29
questions.explanation: With h = 28, B is A with 1 added to every value, so the standard deviations are equal. h = 29 spreads B out more than A. h = 23 pulls the largest value in toward the others, so B's standard deviation is smaller. Only I works.

questions.question: Two lines intersect at exactly one point, forming two acute angles and two obtuse angles. The measure of one of these angles is (9x − 190)°. Which of the following could NOT be the sum of the measures of any two of these angles?
questions.explanation: The angles are 9x − 190 (twice) and 370 − 9x (twice). Possible sums are 18x − 380, 740 − 18x and 180, but not −18x + 380.

questions.question: What is the radius of the circle in the xy−plane defined by (x + 3)2 + (y + 9)2 = 361?
questions.explanation: The circle has the form (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r², so r² = 361 and r = 19.

questions.question: The area of a rectangular region is increasing at a rate of 190 square feet per hour. Which of the following is closest to this rate in <u>square meters per minute</u>? (Use 1 meter = 3.28 feet.)
questions.explanation: 1 square meter = 3.28^2 ≈ 10.76 square feet, so 190 ft^2/hr ≈ 17.66 m^2/hr, and dividing by 60 gives about 0.29 m^2/min.

questions.question: In triangles PQR and XYZ, angles R and Z each have a measure of 38°. The length of side QR is equal to 11. The length of side YZ is equal to 27.5. Which additional piece of information is sufficient to prove that triangle PQR is similar to triangle XYZ?
options: The measure of angle P is 46°
The length of side PR is 14 and the length of side XZ is 35
The measure of angle Q is 49° and the measure of angle Y is 94°
